The deleted phrase was included in the 1827 statute, followed by the clause “or where the prisoner shall be delivered to the constable, or other inferior officer, to be carried to some common jail, or shall be removed from one place to another, within the county, in order to his discharge or trial in due course of law.” (An Act . . . on Writs of Habeas Corpus, p. 326, sec. 11.)

The 1827 statute here included several additional situations in which prisoners could be moved without a writ of habeas corpus, such as removal to an adjoining county if the local jail lacked space or when the prisoner had been “claimed or demanded by the executive of any of the United States or territories” for extradition. These clauses were almost certainly omitted from Nauvoo’s ordinance to further protect JS from extradition to Missouri. (An Act . . . on Writs of Habeas Corpus, p. 326, sec. 11.)
